title.fa: اختیار سارتری از نگاه گومبروویچ: فیلسوف در صندلی راحتی
title.en: Sartrean freedom in Gombrowicz’s eyes: the philosopher in the armchair
title.nl: Sartrean freedom in Gombrowicz’s eyes: the philosopher in the armchair

summary.fa: گومبروویچ اختیار سارتری را دقیق شرح می‌دهد و بعد دو ایراد به آن می‌گیرد: یکی این‌که سارتر برای مرز گذاشتن بر اختیار دلیلی نمی‌آورد، و دیگری این‌که فلسفه‌ای که درد را تحقیر می‌کند فلسفهٔ کسی است که درد نکشیده. ایراد دوم درباره‌ٔ خودِ فیلسوفان است، نه استدلالشان.
summary.en: Gombrowicz expounds Sartrean freedom precisely and then raises two objections: that Sartre gives no reason for the limit he places on freedom, and that a philosophy which despises pain is the philosophy of someone who has not suffered. The second objection is about philosophers themselves, not their arguments.
summary.nl: Gombrowicz expounds Sartrean freedom precisely and then raises two objections: that Sartre gives no reason for the limit he places on freedom, and that a philosophy which despises pain is the philosophy of someone who has not suffered. The second objection is about philosophers themselves, not their arguments.

text.fa: شرح اختیار سارتری: اختیار یک تجربه است و با زمان آینده پیوند دارد؛ آدمی همیشه در وضعیتی است و فقط در آن وضعیت می‌تواند انتخاب کند. مثال خود او: می‌توانم در رختخواب بمانم یا به پیاده‌روی بروم، اما نمی‌توانم پرواز کردن را انتخاب کنم چون بال ندارم.
text.en: The exposition of Sartrean freedom: freedom is an experience bound to the future tense; a person is always in a situation and can choose only within it. His own example: I can stay in bed or go for a walk, but I cannot choose to fly because I have no wings.
text.nl: The exposition of Sartrean freedom: freedom is an experience bound to the future tense; a person is always in a situation and can choose only within it. His own example: I can stay in bed or go for a walk, but I cannot choose to fly because I have no wings.

text.fa: و انتخاب‌نکردن هم انتخاب است: اگر از میان دو امکان هیچ‌کدام را برنگزینم، وضعیت سومی را برگزیده‌ام. کسی که نخواهد میان کمونیسم و ضدکمونیسم یکی را انتخاب کند، خنثی‌بودن را انتخاب کرده است.
text.en: And not choosing is itself a choice: if I choose neither of two possibilities, I have chosen a third position. Whoever refuses to choose between communism and anti-communism has chosen neutrality.
text.nl: And not choosing is itself a choice: if I choose neither of two possibilities, I have chosen a third position. Whoever refuses to choose between communism and anti-communism has chosen neutrality.

text.fa: بنیاد اخلاقی: آن‌که ارزش‌ها را می‌آفریند انسان است، و این نتیجهٔ مستقیم یک بی‌خدایی سرسختانه است — به گفتهٔ گومبروویچ «منسجم‌ترین شکل بی‌خدایی در کل فلسفه». سارتر خودش می‌گفت دنبال کردن بی‌خدایی تا آخرین حدش آسان نیست.
text.en: The ethical foundation: it is man who creates values, and this follows directly from an uncompromising atheism — in Gombrowicz’s words "the most consistent form of atheism in all philosophy." Sartre himself said that following atheism to its last limit is not easy.
text.nl: The ethical foundation: it is man who creates values, and this follows directly from an uncompromising atheism — in Gombrowicz’s words "the most consistent form of atheism in all philosophy." Sartre himself said that following atheism to its last limit is not easy.

text.fa: ایراد اول و منطقی: اگر ما آفرینندهٔ مختار ارزش‌های خودمانیم، چه چیزی مانع می‌شود کسی نظامی هولناک را برای خود برگزیند؟ گومبروویچ می‌گوید این پرسش را از سارتر می‌پرسیدند و او «این تعارض نسبتاً ابتدایی را آن‌چنان‌که باید روشن نکرد»، چون ناگفته پیداست که اخلاق حدی بر اختیار می‌گذارد — ولی آن حد خودش دلیل می‌خواهد.
text.en: The first, logical objection: if we are the free creators of our own values, what prevents anyone from choosing a monstrous order for himself? Gombrowicz says Sartre was asked this and "never properly clarified this rather elementary contradiction," since it is obvious that morality sets a limit on freedom — but that limit itself needs a reason.
text.nl: The first, logical objection: if we are the free creators of our own values, what prevents anyone from choosing a monstrous order for himself? Gombrowicz says Sartre was asked this and "never properly clarified this rather elementary contradiction," since it is obvious that morality sets a limit on freedom — but that limit itself needs a reason.

text.fa: ایراد دوم و شخصی: «به نظر می‌رسد فلاسفه، به استثنای شوپنهاور، افرادی مرفه‌اند که در صندلی راحتی خود لم داده‌اند و با حالتی کاملاً خداگونه درد را تحقیر می‌کنند — رفتاری که با مراجعه به دندان‌پزشک و فریاد "آخ، آخ، دکتر" باد هوا خواهد شد.»
text.en: The second, personal objection: "it seems that philosophers, with the exception of Schopenhauer, are comfortable people lounging in their armchairs and despising pain in an utterly god-like manner — a posture that evaporates at the dentist with a cry of ‘ouch, ouch, doctor’."
text.nl: The second, personal objection: "it seems that philosophers, with the exception of Schopenhauer, are comfortable people lounging in their armchairs and despising pain in an utterly god-like manner — a posture that evaporates at the dentist with a cry of ‘ouch, ouch, doctor’."

text.fa: کاربرد این ایراد بر سارتر: سارتر معتقد بود برای کسی که برمی‌گزیند درد را خوب بشمارد، شکنجه می‌تواند بدل به لذتی آسمانی شود. گومبروویچ این را «بسیار قابل تردید» می‌خواند و ویژگی بورژوازی فرانسوی می‌داند که «در کمال خوشبختی سال‌های سال از دردهای بزرگ در امان بود».
text.en: The objection applied to Sartre: Sartre held that for someone who chooses to count pain as good, torture could become a heavenly pleasure. Gombrowicz calls this "highly dubious" and a trait of a French bourgeoisie that "was happily spared great suffering for years."
text.nl: The objection applied to Sartre: Sartre held that for someone who chooses to count pain as good, torture could become a heavenly pleasure. Gombrowicz calls this "highly dubious" and a trait of a French bourgeoisie that "was happily spared great suffering for years."

text.fa: داوری نهایی او: سارتر همیشه پایی در مارکسیسم (وجه علمی) و پایی در اگزیستانسیالیسم (وجه غیرعلمی) داشت و، مثل دکارت، دچار وحشت شد؛ نتیجه فلسفه‌ای سازشکار شد و «این مرد که از موهبت نبوغی خارق‌العاده برخوردار بود، بدل به انسانی غمگین» شد.
text.en: His final verdict: Sartre always had one foot in Marxism (the scientific side) and one in existentialism (the unscientific side) and, like Descartes, took fright; the result was a compromising philosophy, and "this man, gifted with an extraordinary genius, became a sad man."
text.nl: His final verdict: Sartre always had one foot in Marxism (the scientific side) and one in existentialism (the unscientific side) and, like Descartes, took fright; the result was a compromising philosophy, and "this man, gifted with an extraordinary genius, became a sad man."

text.fa: نکتهٔ فنی که در همین بحث می‌آورد: تفکیک هایدگری ترس از دلهره — «هنگامی که می‌ترسم، از چیزی می‌ترسم، مثلاً از یک ببر؛ اما دلهره زمانی است که از چیز خاصی نمی‌ترسم». به اعتقاد سارتر این دلهره زاییدهٔ مسئولیت ما در قبال وجود خویش است.
text.en: A technical point he makes in the same discussion: Heidegger’s distinction between fear and anxiety — "when I am afraid, I am afraid of something, a tiger for instance; but anxiety is when I fear nothing in particular." For Sartre this anxiety is born of our responsibility for our own existence.
text.nl: A technical point he makes in the same discussion: Heidegger’s distinction between fear and anxiety — "when I am afraid, I am afraid of something, a tiger for instance; but anxiety is when I fear nothing in particular." For Sartre this anxiety is born of our responsibility for our own existence.

text.fa: و یک نقد موردی: سارتر به ژان ژنه دلبسته بود چون ژنه «شر را برگزید». گومبروویچ می‌گوید گفتن چنین چیزی احمقانه است، «زیرا هر رئیس پلیسی خوب می‌داند که ژنه هیچ چیز را انتخاب نکرد» — او با دله‌دزدی شروع کرد و اندک‌اندک، با سازوکاری نامحسوس، دزد شد.
text.en: And a case-level criticism: Sartre was attached to Jean Genet because Genet "chose evil." Gombrowicz calls this foolish, "because any police chief knows perfectly well that Genet chose nothing" — he began with petty theft and became a thief gradually, by an imperceptible mechanism.
text.nl: And a case-level criticism: Sartre was attached to Jean Genet because Genet "chose evil." Gombrowicz calls this foolish, "because any police chief knows perfectly well that Genet chose nothing" — he began with petty theft and became a thief gradually, by an imperceptible mechanism.

text.fa: ایراد دوم او استدلال را رد نمی‌کند، گوینده را هدف می‌گیرد؛ از نظر منطقی این مغالطه است. ارزشش جای دیگری است: پرسش از این‌که فلسفه‌ای که درد را جدی نمی‌گیرد از کدام موقعیت زندگی بیرون آمده.
text.en: His second objection does not refute the argument but targets the speaker; logically that is a fallacy. Its value lies elsewhere: in asking from what position in life a philosophy that does not take pain seriously has emerged.
text.nl: His second objection does not refute the argument but targets the speaker; logically that is a fallacy. Its value lies elsewhere: in asking from what position in life a philosophy that does not take pain seriously has emerged.

note.fa: معیار او: فلسفه باید با زندگی تماس داشته باشد
note.en: His standard: philosophy must touch life
note.nl: His standard: philosophy must touch life

note.fa: آن‌که به نظر او درد را می‌شناخت
note.en: The one who, in his view, knew pain
note.nl: The one who, in his view, knew pain
